title: The Battle of Hastings
description: October 1066. William of Normandy's invasion army faces King Harold's Anglo-Saxon shield wall on Senlac Hill. The player commands the Norman force and must break the shield wall through feigned retreats and combined cavalry-archer assaults before nightfall ends the battle.

anachronisms_found: PIKEMAN x16 on the Anglo-Saxon side: the pike square is a 14th-15th century development; the engine already offers SPEARMAN (used here for the fyrd), so massed pikemen for 1066 levies was avoidable
GUARD_TOWER x2 for the Saxons: Harold's host reached Senlac Hill only days before and fought behind a shield wall, not stone fortifications; a Palisade or nothing would have been truer

TOWN_CENTER x1 for each side on the battlefield itself, plus STABLE, ARCHERY_RANGE, BLACKSMITH and BARRACKS: a full economic/production base is out of place for an invasion army camped at Hastings and an Anglo-Saxon field host; only the PAVILION_A/TENT_A camps are appropriate
MONASTERY for Player Two on Senlac Hill: Battle Abbey was founded on the site only after 1070, so a monastery present during the battle is inverted chronology
CROSSBOWMAN x6: Norman crossbows at Hastings are only weakly attested and the AoE2 Crossbowman represents a later, heavier weapon; ARCHER alone would have been safer

4,480 TREE_OAK on a 120x120 map: Senlac was open downland with the ridge as the decisive terrain feature; blanketing the map in oak forest misrepresents the ground on which the cavalry charges and feigned retreats occurred

issues_found: Both players are set to RANDOM civilization, so the Norman and Anglo-Saxon sides may render with Mesoamerican, East Asian or Middle Eastern architecture and unit skins — an avoidable error since Franks/Britons/Teutons were available and would give period-plausible European buildings.

Player 1 fields CROSSBOWMAN x6 alongside archers; the crossbow is essentially absent from the 1066 Norman host (the Bayeux Tapestry shows self-bows), and plain ARCHER units were already available for the whole contingent.
Player 2 has a MONASTERY and GUARD_TOWER x2 on Senlac Hill; Harold's army arrived after a forced march and fortified nothing there — no towers or religious houses stood on the ridge.

4,480 oak trees on a 120x120 map makes the field a near-continuous forest, whereas the decisive ground was an open ridge and slope; the Andredsweald lay behind the Saxon line, not across the battlefield.
Harold's KING unit is a bare generic king rather than a renamed stand-in identified as Harold Godwinson in the object list, so his identity rests entirely on dialogue rather than placement.
No Anglo-Saxon missile troops or thegn-quality axemen distinct from the fyrd beyond CHAMPION x6; the housecarl/fyrd distinction is thin, and the deaths of Gyrth and Leofwine are absent.

Both players are set to RANDOM civilization, so architecture, unit skins and bonuses could resolve to Aztec, Japanese or Mongol styling for the Normans and Anglo-Saxons alike — an entirely avoidable omission given Franks/Britons/Teutons are available.
4,480 TREE_OAK on a 120x120 map makes Senlac Hill a dense forest; the historical field was an open slope with the Andredsweald woodland only behind the Saxon line.
GOLD_MINE x5, STONE_MINE x4, FORAGE_BUSH x8, SHEEP x6 and a TOWN_CENTER for each side import economic furniture into what was a single-day set-piece battle with no settlement present.
CROSSBOWMAN x6 for the Norman side overstates the crossbow at Hastings; the sources describe bowmen, and the engine's ARCHER already covers them.
PIKEMAN x16 in the Saxon shield wall is a late-medieval unit where SPEARMAN/MILITIA-line units would have represented the fyrd and housecarls without anachronism.
Harold is represented by the generic KING unit rather than a renamed infantry unit; the king unit is unarmed and non-combatant, so the man who died fighting in the line cannot fight.
